# Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA)

## CRITICAL RULES

1. **Minimum 15 samples required.** WGCNA will produce unreliable results with fewer. If the user has <15, warn them and suggest differential expression instead.
2. **Input must be normalized expression** (VST, TPM, FPKM, log-CPM). Do NOT use raw counts — WGCNA assumes approximately normally distributed data.
3. **Session persistence**: Each `execute_code` runs in a separate R session. Save all objects with `saveRDS()` and reload in the next step.
4. **Always show the soft-threshold plot** to the user and confirm the power value before building the network. Do NOT auto-pick without showing.
5. **Figures**: PNG only, 150 DPI, white background (`bg = "white"`).
6. **Signed network by default** — use `networkType = "signed"` unless the user specifically requests unsigned.

---

## Triggers
WGCNA, gene co-expression network, module detection, hub genes, eigengene, soft threshold, module-trait, gene network modules, weighted correlation network

---

## Input Requirements

| Input | Required | Format |
|-------|----------|--------|
| Expression matrix | Yes | CSV/TSV — genes as rows, samples as columns (or transposed) |
| Trait / metadata file | Optional | CSV — samples as rows, traits as columns (numeric or categorical) |

- Expression values must be **normalized** (VST from DESeq2, TPM, FPKM, or log-CPM)
- If the user provides raw counts, run VST normalization first using DESeq2

---

## Workflow

### Step 1: Load & Prepare Data

```r
library(WGCNA)
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
allowWGCNAThreads()

# --- Load expression matrix ---
expr <- read.csv("expression_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)

# Ensure genes=rows, samples=columns; then transpose for WGCNA (needs samples=rows)
# Heuristic: if ncol >> nrow, it's likely already samples×genes
if (nrow(expr) > ncol(expr)) {
  datExpr <- as.data.frame(t(expr))
} else {
  datExpr <- as.data.frame(expr)
}

cat("Samples:", nrow(datExpr), "\nGenes:", ncol(datExpr), "\n")

if (nrow(datExpr) < 15) {
  stop("WGCNA requires >=15 samples. Found only ", nrow(datExpr))
}

# --- Filter low-variance genes ---
gene_var <- apply(datExpr, 2, var)
keep <- gene_var > quantile(gene_var, 0.25)  # keep top 75% by variance
datExpr <- datExpr[, keep]
cat("Genes after variance filter:", ncol(datExpr), "\n")

# --- Check for outlier samples ---
sampleTree <- hclust(dist(datExpr), method = "average")
png("sample_dendrogram.png", width = 1200, height = 600, res = 150, bg = "white")
par(mar = c(2, 6, 2, 2))
plot(sampleTree, main = "Sample Clustering to Detect Outliers",
     sub = "", xlab = "", cex.lab = 1.2, cex = 0.7)
# Draw a cut line at a reasonable height (user can adjust)
abline(h = max(sampleTree$height) * 0.9, col = "red", lty = 2)
dev.off()

# --- Check for genes/samples with too many missing values ---
gsg <- goodSamplesGenes(datExpr, verbose = 3)
if (!gsg$allOK) {
  datExpr <- datExpr[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes]
  cat("Removed bad samples/genes. Remaining:", nrow(datExpr), "samples,", ncol(datExpr), "genes\n")
}

saveRDS(datExpr, "datExpr.rds")
cat("Data prepared and saved.\n")
```

### Step 2: Pick Soft Threshold

```r
library(WGCNA)

datExpr <- readRDS("datExpr.rds")

# Test a range of soft-thresholding powers
powers <- c(1:20)
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(datExpr, powerVector = powers,
                         networkType = "signed", verbose = 5)

saveRDS(sft, "soft_threshold.rds")

# --- Plot scale-free topology fit & mean connectivity ---
png("soft_threshold_plot.png", width = 1200, height = 600, res = 150, bg = "white")
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Scale-free topology fit
plot(sft$fitIndices[, 1], -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],
     xlab = "Soft Threshold (power)",
     ylab = "Scale Free Topology Model Fit (signed R²)",
     main = "Scale Independence", type = "n")
text(sft$fitIndices[, 1], -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],
     labels = powers, col = "red")
abline(h = 0.85, col = "blue", lty = 2)

# Mean connectivity
plot(sft$fitIndices[, 1], sft$fitIndices[, 5],
     xlab = "Soft Threshold (power)",
     ylab = "Mean Connectivity",
     main = "Mean Connectivity", type = "n")
text(sft$fitIndices[, 1], sft$fitIndices[, 5], labels = powers, col = "red")
dev.off()

# Report recommended power
if (!is.na(sft$powerEstimate)) {
  cat("Recommended soft-threshold power:", sft$powerEstimate, "\n")
} else {
  cat("No power reached R² > 0.85. Consider:\n")
  cat("  - Using the power where R² is highest (check plot)\n")
  cat("  - Trying a signed hybrid network\n")
  cat("  - Filtering more genes\n")
}
```

**STOP here and show the user the soft-threshold plot.** Confirm the power value before proceeding.

### Step 3: Build Network & Detect Modules

```r
library(WGCNA)

datExpr <- readRDS("datExpr.rds")
sft <- readRDS("soft_threshold.rds")

# Use the chosen power (from Step 2)
softPower <- sft$powerEstimate  # or user-specified value

net <- blockwiseModules(
  datExpr,
  power = softPower,
  networkType = "signed",
  TOMType = "signed",
  minModuleSize = 30,
  reassignThreshold = 0,
  mergeCutHeight = 0.25,    # merge modules with >75% correlation
  numericLabels = TRUE,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  saveTOMs = FALSE,          # save memory
  verbose = 3
)

# Convert numeric labels to colors
moduleColors <- labels2colors(net$colors)
cat("Modules detected:", length(unique(moduleColors)), "\n")
cat(table(moduleColors), "\n")

# --- Plot module dendrogram ---
png("module_dendrogram.png", width = 1400, height = 700, res = 150, bg = "white")
plotDendroAndColors(net$dendrograms[[1]], moduleColors[net$blockGenes[[1]]],
                    "Module colors",
                    dendroLabels = FALSE, hang = 0.03,
                    addGuide = TRUE, guideHang = 0.05,
                    main = "Gene Dendrogram and Module Colors")
dev.off()

saveRDS(net, "wgcna_network.rds")
saveRDS(moduleColors, "moduleColors.rds")
cat("Network built and saved.\n")
```

### Step 4: Module–Trait Correlation

Skip this step if the user has no trait/metadata file.

```r
library(WGCNA)
library(ggplot2)

datExpr <- readRDS("datExpr.rds")
net <- readRDS("wgcna_network.rds")
moduleColors <- readRDS("moduleColors.rds")

# --- Load trait data ---
traits <- read.csv("traits.csv", row.names = 1)

# Make sure samples match
common <- intersect(rownames(datExpr), rownames(traits))
datExpr <- datExpr[common, ]
traits <- traits[common, , drop = FALSE]

# Convert categorical traits to numeric (dummy encoding)
for (col in colnames(traits)) {
  if (!is.numeric(traits[[col]])) {
    traits[[col]] <- as.numeric(as.factor(traits[[col]]))
  }
}

# --- Compute module eigengenes ---
MEs <- moduleEigengenes(datExpr, colors = moduleColors)$eigengenes
MEs <- orderMEs(MEs)

# --- Correlate eigengenes with traits ---
modTraitCor <- cor(MEs, traits, use = "p")
modTraitPval <- corPvalueStudent(modTraitCor, nrow(datExpr))

# --- Heatmap ---
textMatrix <- paste0(signif(modTraitCor, 2), "\n(",
                     signif(modTraitPval, 1), ")")
dim(textMatrix) <- dim(modTraitCor)

png("module_trait_heatmap.png", width = max(800, ncol(traits) * 200),
    height = max(600, nrow(modTraitCor) * 40 + 200), res = 150, bg = "white")
par(mar = c(6, 10, 3, 2))
labeledHeatmap(Matrix = modTraitCor,
               xLabels = colnames(traits),
               yLabels = names(MEs),
               ySymbols = names(MEs),
               colorLabels = FALSE,
               colors = blueWhiteRed(50),
               textMatrix = textMatrix,
               setStdMargins = FALSE,
               cex.text = 0.6,
               zlim = c(-1, 1),
               main = "Module-Trait Relationships")
dev.off()

# --- Save correlation table ---
cor_df <- as.data.frame(modTraitCor)
cor_df$module <- rownames(cor_df)
write.csv(cor_df, "module_trait_correlations.csv", row.names = FALSE)

saveRDS(MEs, "module_eigengenes.rds")
cat("Module-trait correlations computed.\n")
```

### Step 5: Hub Genes & Visualization

```r
library(WGCNA)
library(igraph)

datExpr <- readRDS("datExpr.rds")
net <- readRDS("wgcna_network.rds")
moduleColors <- readRDS("moduleColors.rds")

# --- Intramodular connectivity (kME) ---
MEs <- moduleEigengenes(datExpr, colors = moduleColors)$eigengenes

kME <- signedKME(datExpr, MEs)
colnames(kME) <- gsub("^kME", "", colnames(kME))

# --- Hub genes per module: top 10 by kME ---
hub_list <- list()
for (mod in unique(moduleColors)) {
  mod_genes <- colnames(datExpr)[moduleColors == mod]
  kme_col <- paste0("ME", mod)
  if (kme_col %in% colnames(MEs)) {
    kme_vals <- kME[mod_genes, mod]
    top <- head(sort(kme_vals, decreasing = TRUE), 10)
    hub_list[[mod]] <- data.frame(
      gene = names(top),
      module = mod,
      kME = round(as.numeric(top), 4)
    )
  }
}
hub_genes <- do.call(rbind, hub_list)
write.csv(hub_genes, "hub_genes.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Top hub genes per module saved.\n")

# --- Network plot for top module ---
# Pick the largest non-grey module
mod_sizes <- table(moduleColors)
mod_sizes <- mod_sizes[names(mod_sizes) != "grey"]
top_mod <- names(which.max(mod_sizes))

mod_genes <- colnames(datExpr)[moduleColors == top_mod]
# Subset to top 50 hub genes for visibility
kme_col <- paste0("ME", top_mod)
kme_vals <- kME[mod_genes, top_mod]
top50 <- names(head(sort(kme_vals, decreasing = TRUE), 50))

# Compute adjacency for these genes
adj <- adjacency(datExpr[, top50], power = net$power, type = "signed")
diag(adj) <- 0
adj[adj < 0.1] <- 0  # threshold for cleaner plot

# Build igraph
g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(as.matrix(adj), mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE)
V(g)$size <- scales::rescale(kme_vals[top50], to = c(3, 12))
V(g)$label.cex <- 0.5
E(g)$width <- E(g)$weight * 3

png("network_top_module.png", width = 1200, height = 1200, res = 150, bg = "white")
plot(g, layout = layout_with_fr(g),
     vertex.color = top_mod,
     vertex.frame.color = NA,
     edge.color = adjustcolor("grey60", alpha.f = 0.4),
     main = paste0("Co-expression Network: ", top_mod, " module (top 50 genes)"))
dev.off()

cat("Network visualization saved.\n")
```

### Step 6: Export Results

```r
library(WGCNA)

datExpr <- readRDS("datExpr.rds")
net <- readRDS("wgcna_network.rds")
moduleColors <- readRDS("moduleColors.rds")
MEs <- readRDS("module_eigengenes.rds")

# --- Module assignments ---
module_df <- data.frame(
  gene = colnames(datExpr),
  module = moduleColors,
  module_number = net$colors
)
write.csv(module_df, "module_assignments.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# --- Eigengene matrix ---
eigen_df <- as.data.frame(MEs)
eigen_df$sample <- rownames(eigen_df)
eigen_df <- eigen_df[, c("sample", setdiff(colnames(eigen_df), "sample"))]
write.csv(eigen_df, "module_eigengenes.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# --- Save full WGCNA object ---
saveRDS(net, "wgcna_full_results.rds")

cat("All results exported.\n")
```

## Output Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `sample_dendrogram.png` | Hierarchical clustering to detect outlier samples |
| `soft_threshold_plot.png` | Scale-free topology fit & mean connectivity vs. power |
| `module_dendrogram.png` | Gene dendrogram with module color assignments |
| `module_trait_heatmap.png` | Module–trait correlation heatmap (if traits provided) |

| `module_assignments.csv` | Gene → module mapping for all genes |
| `hub_genes.csv` | Top 10 hub genes per module with kME values |
| `module_eigengenes.csv` | Eigengene values per sample per module |
| `module_trait_correlations.csv` | Correlation + p-value of each module vs. each trait |
| `wgcna_full_results.rds` | Full WGCNA network object for follow-up analysis |

---

## Edge Cases & Troubleshooting

| Situation | Solution |
|-----------|----------|
| Fewer than 15 samples | WGCNA is unreliable — suggest DE analysis instead |
| No soft threshold reaches R² > 0.85 | Use the power with highest R², try signed hybrid network (`networkType = "signed hybrid"`), or filter more low-variance genes |
| All/most genes in one module | Lower `mergeCutHeight` (e.g., 0.15), increase `minModuleSize`, or filter more genes |
| Too many small modules | Increase `mergeCutHeight` (e.g., 0.35) to merge similar modules |
| Grey module is very large | Grey = unassigned genes. This is normal for noisy genes. Lower `minModuleSize` if needed |
| Memory issues with >20K genes | Filter to top 5000–10000 most variable genes before WGCNA |
| Raw counts provided | Run VST normalization first: `vsd <- vst(dds); datExpr <- t(assay(vsd))` |
| Samples don't match between expression and traits | Use `intersect()` to align — shown in Step 4 |
| User wants unsigned network | Set `networkType = "unsigned"`, `TOMType = "unsigned"` in `blockwiseModules()` |

name: wgs-alignment
description: Align WGS/WES paired-end reads to a reference genome using BWA-MEM2 with GATK best practices

# WGS/WES Alignment

## Triggers
WGS, WES, whole genome sequencing, whole exome sequencing, BWA, BWA-MEM2, genomic alignment, DNA-seq, exome sequencing, DNA alignment, FASTQ to BAM

---

## CRITICAL RULES

1. **If the organism is in the S3 index table below, ALWAYS download the pre-built BWA index.** NEVER run `bwa-mem2 index` for these organisms.
2. **Default aligner is BWA-MEM2.** It is a drop-in replacement for BWA-MEM with identical output but 2-3x faster.
3. **Always store indexes in `/tmp/indexes/`** (NOT EFS, NOT the working directory).
4. **Never re-download** an index if it already exists — check first.
5. **Mark duplicates with Picard** unless the user explicitly says not to.
6. **For variant calling downstream**, tell the user to load the `variant-calling` skill after alignment.

---

## Pre-built Indexes on S3

All indexes are at `s3://pipettebio-public-resources/`. Download with `--no-sign-request`.

| Organism | BWA-MEM2 Index | Genome FASTA |
|----------|---------------|--------------|
| Human GRCh38 | `bwa-mem2/humans/grch38/index/` | `bwa-mem2/humans/grch38/genome/genome.fa.gz` |
| Mouse GRCm38 | `bwa-mem2/mouse/grcm38/index/` | `bwa-mem2/mouse/grcm38/genome/genome.fa.gz` |

**Index subdirectory structure:**
- `bwa-mem2/{organism}/index/` — BWA-MEM2 index files (`.0123`, `.amb`, `.ann`, `.bwt.2bit.64`, `.pac`)
- `bwa-mem2/{organism}/genome/` — reference FASTA (genome.fa.gz)

**If the user's organism is NOT in this table**, you must build the index yourself:
```bash
# Download genome FASTA from Ensembl/NCBI
bwa-mem2 index -p /tmp/indexes/bwa-mem2/custom/genome genome.fa
```

---

## Resource Configuration

| Step | Threads | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| fastp (trimming) | 16 | One sample at a time (WGS files are large) |
| BWA-MEM2 | 14 | Reserve 2 cores for samtools sort piped |
| samtools sort | 4 | Piped from BWA-MEM2, uses 2GB memory per thread |
| samtools index | 4 | After sorting |
| Picard MarkDuplicates | 1 | Single-threaded, ~8GB heap |

---

## Workflow

### Step 1: Download BWA-MEM2 Index from S3
```bash
INDEX_DIR="/tmp/indexes/bwa-mem2/humans/grch38"
GENOME_DIR="/tmp/indexes/bwa-mem2/humans/grch38/genome"
mkdir -p $INDEX_DIR $GENOME_DIR

# Check if already downloaded
if [ ! -f "$INDEX_DIR/genome.fa.bwt.2bit.64" ]; then
    aws s3 sync s3://pipettebio-public-resources/bwa-mem2/humans/grch38/index/ $INDEX_DIR/ --no-sign-request
    aws s3 sync s3://pipettebio-public-resources/bwa-mem2/humans/grch38/genome/ $GENOME_DIR/ --no-sign-request
    # Decompress genome if needed
    if [ -f "$GENOME_DIR/genome.fa.gz" ] && [ ! -f "$GENOME_DIR/genome.fa" ]; then
        gunzip -k $GENOME_DIR/genome.fa.gz
    fi
fi

# Verify
ls $INDEX_DIR/*.bwt.2bit.64  # Must exist
ls $GENOME_DIR/genome.fa      # Must exist
```

### Step 2: Trim Reads (fastp)
```bash
mkdir -p trimmed qc

fastp \
    -i sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    -I sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    -o trimmed/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    -O trimmed/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    --thread 16 \
    --detect_adapter_for_pe \
    --qualified_quality_phred 20 \
    --length_required 50 \
    --html qc/sample_fastp.html \
    --json qc/sample_fastp.json
```

### Step 3: Align with BWA-MEM2 + Sort
```bash
mkdir -p alignments

SAMPLE="sample"
RGID="${SAMPLE}"
RGSM="${SAMPLE}"
RGPL="ILLUMINA"
RGLB="lib1"

bwa-mem2 mem -t 14 \
    -R "@RG\tID:${RGID}\tSM:${RGSM}\tPL:${RGPL}\tLB:${RGLB}" \
    $INDEX_DIR/genome.fa \
    trimmed/${SAMPLE}_R1.fastq.gz \
    trimmed/${SAMPLE}_R2.fastq.gz \
  | samtools sort -@ 4 -m 2G -o alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam

samtools index -@ 4 alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam
```

**Read Group tags are REQUIRED for GATK.** Always add `-R` with at minimum ID, SM, PL, LB.

### Step 4: Mark Duplicates (Picard)
```bash
java -Xmx8g -jar $PICARD_JAR MarkDuplicates \
    I=alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam \
    O=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam \
    M=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup_metrics.txt \
    REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false \
    CREATE_INDEX=true

# Or if picard is installed as a command:
picard MarkDuplicates \
    I=alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam \
    O=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam \
    M=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup_metrics.txt \
    REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false \
    CREATE_INDEX=true
```

### Step 5: Alignment QC
```bash
# Flagstat
samtools flagstat alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam > alignments/${SAMPLE}.flagstat.txt

# Coverage stats (WGS)
samtools depth -a alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam | \
    awk '{sum+=$3; cnt++} END {print "Mean depth:", sum/cnt}' > alignments/${SAMPLE}.depth.txt

# Insert size metrics
picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics \
    I=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam \
    O=alignments/${SAMPLE}.insert_size_metrics.txt \
    H=alignments/${SAMPLE}.insert_size_histogram.pdf
```

### Step 6: (Optional) Base Quality Score Recalibration — GATK BQSR

Only needed if the user plans variant calling with GATK. Requires known sites VCF.

```bash
# Download known sites (human GRCh38)
KNOWN_SITES="/tmp/indexes/gatk_resources"
mkdir -p $KNOWN_SITES
# User must provide or download dbSNP + Mills + 1000G known sites

gatk BaseRecalibrator \
    -I alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam \
    -R $GENOME_DIR/genome.fa \
    --known-sites $KNOWN_SITES/dbsnp.vcf.gz \
    --known-sites $KNOWN_SITES/Mills_and_1000G.vcf.gz \
    -O alignments/${SAMPLE}.recal_data.table

gatk ApplyBQSR \
    -I alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam \
    -R $GENOME_DIR/genome.fa \
    --bqsr-recal-file alignments/${SAMPLE}.recal_data.table \
    -O alignments/${SAMPLE}.bqsr.bam
```

---

## Multiple Samples

For multiple samples, loop over each:
```bash
for SAMPLE in sample1 sample2 sample3; do
    # Steps 2-5 for each sample (run sequentially — WGS files are large)
    fastp -i ${SAMPLE}_R1.fastq.gz -I ${SAMPLE}_R2.fastq.gz \
          -o trimmed/${SAMPLE}_R1.fastq.gz -O trimmed/${SAMPLE}_R2.fastq.gz \
          --thread 16 --detect_adapter_for_pe --html qc/${SAMPLE}_fastp.html

    bwa-mem2 mem -t 14 \
        -R "@RG\tID:${SAMPLE}\tSM:${SAMPLE}\tPL:ILLUMINA\tLB:lib1" \
        $INDEX_DIR/genome.fa \
        trimmed/${SAMPLE}_R1.fastq.gz trimmed/${SAMPLE}_R2.fastq.gz \
      | samtools sort -@ 4 -m 2G -o alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam

    samtools index -@ 4 alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam

    picard MarkDuplicates \
        I=alignments/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam \
        O=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam \
        M=alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup_metrics.txt \
        REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false CREATE_INDEX=true

    samtools flagstat alignments/${SAMPLE}.dedup.bam > alignments/${SAMPLE}.flagstat.txt
done
```

---

## Required Outputs

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `alignments/{sample}.dedup.bam` | Sorted, deduplicated BAM |
| `alignments/{sample}.dedup.bam.bai` | BAM index |
| `alignments/{sample}.dedup_metrics.txt` | Duplicate rate metrics |
| `alignments/{sample}.flagstat.txt` | Alignment summary stats |
| `qc/{sample}_fastp.html` | Trimming QC report |

---

## Quality Thresholds

| Metric | Good | Investigate |
|--------|------|-------------|
| Mapping rate | >95% | <90% (contamination? wrong reference?) |
| Properly paired | >90% | <80% |
| Duplicate rate (WGS) | 5-15% | >30% (low library complexity) |
| Duplicate rate (WES) | 10-30% | >50% |
| Mean depth (WGS 30x) | 25-35x | <20x |
| Mean depth (WES) | 50-100x | <30x |
| Insert size | 200-500bp | Bimodal or very broad |

---

## Edge Cases

| Situation | Solution |
|-----------|----------|
| Single-end reads | Drop `-I` from fastp, use only R1 in BWA-MEM2, remove `--countReadPairs` |
| Very large WGS (>100GB FASTQ) | Process one sample at a time, not parallel |
| User wants CRAM instead of BAM | Add `samtools view -C -T genome.fa -o sample.cram sample.bam` |
| Organism not in S3 table | Download genome from Ensembl, build index with `bwa-mem2 index` |
| User has pre-trimmed reads | Skip Step 2 |
| BQSR known sites not available | Skip BQSR — mention that variant quality may be slightly lower |
| User asks for variant calling | Tell them to load the `variant-calling` skill after alignment |

---

## Related Skills
- **variant-calling**: Call germline variants from the BAM files produced here
- **somatic-variants**: Call somatic mutations (needs tumor + normal BAMs)
- **cnv-analysis**: Detect copy number variations from BAM files
